output.hypothesis: Past campaigns show that highlighting Allbirds' signature natural materials (wool, tree fiber, sugarcane) and their soft, breathable comfort drives email signups among runners and walkers, and that performance data will confirm which platform-asset combos (Newsletter vs X, static vs video) convert best for launch lead-gen.

calls.reason: Understand previous launch campaigns' goals, editorial scores, and what evidence gaps/claims existed so we don't repeat mistakes.
Identify which material or comfort claims previously failed verification so we only use substantiated messaging.
See the brand's overall claim verification track record by claim type to calibrate risk tolerance for the new launch.
Learn which content formats on Newsletter and X historically generated the highest signup conversion rates.
Retrieve previously captured source sections that substantiate Allbirds' core material and comfort claims for reuse in launch assets.
Discover what Hacker News discussions about Allbirds reveal regarding runner/walker priorities and language to mirror in signup CTAs.

decisions.statement: Do not make capability claims about what the newsletter will deliver (e.g., confirmed updates, pre‑launch guidance) without a primary source.
decisions.rationale: A capability claim that the newsletter would provide confirmed updates and practical pre‑launch guidance was found unsupported and had to be repaired in the previous campaign (unsupported_claims#2).

decisions.statement: Avoid time‑bound claims about the upcoming running shoe’s construction, fit, price, availability, or performance unless the official release has been verified and cited.
decisions.rationale: A time‑bound claim that those details were unconfirmed conflicted with the official Allbirds release and was flagged as a conflict (unsupported_claims#1).

decisions.statement: Treat framing and opinion claims as editorial‑only; do not present them as verifiable facts.
decisions.rationale: Across recent campaigns, 40 framing claims and 4 opinion claims were marked editorial and required no repair, showing they are acceptable only as styled copy, not as evidence‑backed assertions (claim_risk#2, claim_risk#3).

decisions.statement: Lead with the verified material stack — Merino wool, TENCEL™ Lyocell (tree fiber), sugarcane‑based SweetFoam® — and the specific comfort benefits (breathable, moisture‑wicking, energy return) documented in prior assets.
decisions.rationale: Prior campaign assets contain quoted, source‑tagged excerpts for wool, tree fiber, and SweetFoam® with direct consumer‑facing benefit language (prior_evidence#5, prior_evidence#8, prior_evidence#9).

decisions.statement: Reuse the “Everyday Walks • Vacation • Happy Hour” use‑case framing and the 8.7 oz / 6.7 oz weight specs from the Men’s Cruiser page to ground the running shoe in familiar, verified scenarios.
decisions.rationale: The same prior campaign includes the exact use‑case tags and technical weights used in Allbirds’ own product copy (prior_evidence#6).

decisions.statement: Address current newsletter subscribers and high‑intent site visitors first; they already know the material story and are the most likely to convert to a running‑shoe waitlist.
decisions.rationale: The brief’s explicit goal is growing email signups ahead of launch, and the brand’s own copy positions shoes for daily routines, weekend plans, and travel — behaviors typical of existing subscribers (fact:fact-21, fact:fact-25).

decisions.statement: Frame the launch around material innovation (wool, tree fiber, sugarcane SweetFoam®) translated into running‑specific comfort: breathable, lightweight, responsive energy return.
decisions.rationale: World facts confirm Allbirds replaces petroleum synthetics with these natural materials and calls them soft, breathable, and better for the planet (fact:fact-3, fact:fact-14, fact:fact-19), and prior evidence ties SweetFoam® to energy return (prior_evidence#9).

decisions.statement: Prioritize the owned newsletter channel for depth and conversion; use X only for teaser threads that drive sign‑ups.
decisions.rationale: The brief lists Newsletter first and X second; no performance data exists to reorder them, so follow the brief’s hierarchy.

openQuestions: What are the confirmed construction, fit, price, availability, and performance details of the new running shoe from the official Allbirds release?
Are there any recent email‑capture benchmarks (open rate, click‑through, signup conversion) for Allbirds newsletters that should shape frequency or incentive strategy?

decisions.statement: Do not publish specific construction, fit, price, availability, or performance details for the upcoming running shoe until they are confirmed by an official Allbirds release.
decisions.rationale: A time‑bound claim that those details were unconfirmed was contradicted by the official release (unsupported_claims#1, claim_risk#7), so any unapproved specs risk a conflict status.

decisions.statement: Only promise newsletter benefits (e.g., confirmed updates, pre‑launch guidance) that are backed by a primary source such as the brand’s own signup page or press release.
decisions.rationale: A capability claim about the newsletter’s value was unsupported and had to be repaired (unsupported_claims#2, claim_risk#8); unsupported promises trigger editorial flags.

decisions.statement: Lead with verified material facts — Merino wool, TENCEL™ Lyocell (tree fiber), sugarcane‑based SweetFoam® — and their comfort/breathability benefits from the brand’s own product pages.
decisions.rationale: Multiple world facts (fact:fact-3, fact:fact-13, fact:fact-14, fact:fact-15, fact:fact-19) and prior evidence (prior_evidence#5, #8, #9) confirm these materials and their soft, breathable, energy‑return properties.

decisions.statement: Frame the shoe for daily routines, weekend plans, travel, and casual occasions using the brand’s own “everyday” language.
decisions.rationale: World facts (fact:fact-21, fact:fact-25, fact:fact-27, fact:fact-29, fact:fact-30, fact:fact-31) and prior evidence (prior_evidence#4, #6) consistently position Allbirds for everyday walks, vacations, and happy hours.

decisions.statement: Position the new running shoe as the evolution of Allbirds’ natural‑material comfort (wool, tree fiber, sugarcane foam) into a performance running silhouette.
decisions.rationale: Verified material innovations (fact:fact-3, fact:fact-14, fact:fact-19, prior_evidence#5, #9) and the brand’s everyday‑wear positioning (fact:fact-21, fact:fact-31) together support a “material innovation meets everyday performance” narrative.

decisions.statement: Target runners and everyday walkers who prioritize comfort and natural materials; exclude sustainability‑only messaging that lacks product proof.
decisions.rationale: The brief defines this audience; world facts confirm comfort/material attributes (fact:fact-3, fact:fact-13, fact:fact-15) and everyday use (fact:fact-21, fact:fact-31), while the SEC action on the “sustainable” label (fact:fact-29) warns against unsubstantiated green claims.

decisions.statement: Do not reference funding rounds, IPO, reverse stock split, IP sale, or AI infrastructure pivot in newsletter or X copy.
decisions.rationale: Those events (fact:fact-27, fact:fact-28, fact:fact-30, fact:fact-31, audience_signals#1, audience_signals#2) are unrelated to the shoe launch and distract from the comfort/material angle.

decisions.statement: Open question: No performance data exists for Newsletter or X assets; gather historic open/click rates and X engagement before finalizing channel weight or format mix.
decisions.rationale: The performance tool returned zero rows, so no evidence supports prioritizing one channel over the other beyond the brief’s listing order.
